page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 CPU model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It does not support hyperthreading, ensuring dedicated CPU allocation per vCPU via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via hardware-assisted AES, though other advanced vector or matrix extensions are absent.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2009.48, placing it in the average tier. Multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 4001.26, reflecting the low core count of this specific size. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture and dedicated core allocation provide a predictable compute profile for lightweight workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading.

The c9g.large is suited for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have low memory footprints. Appropriate use cases include lightweight web serving, microservices, containerized applications, and basic CI/CD pipeline tasks that benefit from single-threaded efficiency.
